3| // stageChunk writes one backfill chunk into the staging segment and
4| // hands it to the flush path. Chunk sizing is owned by the backfill
5| // planner; staging only enforces that a chunk arrives whole, because
6| // a partial chunk after a crash would replay rows twice.
7| func (b *Backfill) stageChunk(c Chunk) error {
8| 	if err := c.complete(); err != nil {
9| 		return err
10| 	}
11| 	seg := b.staging.current()
12| 	if err := seg.append(c); err != nil {
13| 		return err
14| 	}
15| 	return b.flusher.enqueue(seg)
16| }

1| package replay
2| 
3| // assembleColumns turns a staged chunk into the columnar layout the
4| // exporter consumes. Column vectors are built per field with nulls
5| // tracked in a validity bitmap; the assembly is allocation-heavy on
6| // purpose at this layer so the flush path below it stays copy-free.
7| func assembleColumns(c Chunk) (ColumnSet, error) {
8| 	fields := c.schema.Fields()
9| 	out := make(ColumnSet, len(fields))
10| 	for i, f := range fields {
11| 		vec, err := buildVector(c, f)
12| 		if err != nil {
13| 			return nil, err
14| 		}
15| 		out[i] = vec
16| 	}
17| 	return out, nil
18| }
19| 
20| // buildVector walks one field across the chunk's rows. Validity is a
21| // bitmap rather than a sentinel value because sentinel collisions
22| // with real data were the root cause of the rewrite's ugliest
23| // pre-merge bug, and the bitmap makes absence unrepresentable as a
24| // value.
25| func buildVector(c Chunk, f Field) (Vector, error) {
26| 	v := newVector(f.Type, c.rows())
27| 	for i := 0; i < c.rows(); i++ {
28| 		cell, ok := c.cell(i, f)
29| 		if !ok {
30| 			v.setNull(i)
31| 			continue
32| 		}
33| 		if err := v.set(i, cell); err != nil {
34| 			return Vector{}, err
35| 		}
36| 	}
37| 	return v, nil
38| }
